sentences.text: Researchers constructed a detailed map of the human basal ganglia by combining two sequencing technologies on tissue from four healthy individuals, addressing a previous lack of complete knowledge regarding cell types and their precise arrangement in this region.

The study revealed that specific neuron and non-neuronal cell types exhibited unique molecular and location patterns, where RNA positioning indicated cell body size and connection direction, and certain support cells clustered at zone boundaries while a specific interneuron type resided within only one zone.
Comparisons with other primates indicated that while some brain structures share similar organization across species, other details remain unique to humans, as the authors concluded.
